reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the plan still needed revising in the last round (round 3 of 3). I read run/mod.rs (dispatch, check_and_verify, the NoCi call at lines 1264-1275), ci_result.rs (Wait, read_ci, resolve), gh/early.rs, gh/client.rs and ci.yml. The plan's design is sound. Choosing the source and the wait together in `with_ci_source` stops a no-remote job from sitting through the 25-minute wait over `NoCi`. Only the `gh::Runner` is faked, so the production `GhClient::ci_source` query is what the tests exercise. The forced push handles a branch left over from a killed job. The delete sits in `dispatch` after the `RunContext` is built, so on the reread path only the inner call deletes, and it deletes once. The ci.yml `history` job runs on pushes too and would fail on a candidate, but g437's `aggregate_verdict` already judges by the aggregate job (client.rs:548), so that is handled. One real gap remains. The criterion 1–3 tests set `origin` to `https://github.com/example/project.git`. `check_and_verify` calls `early_pr` at line 1201 for that origin, and outside `early_seam` it uses `GhCli` and a real `git push`. The plan never installs `early_seam`, so its main demonstrations would make real network calls, which the request forbids, and could hang or flake. The other findings are minor. Findings: major: The CI tests with a github.com https origin would also trigger the real early pull request, which means real network calls. (Demonstrations, criteria 1–3; step 10; crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs:1201; crates/athena-core/src/gh/early.rs:321-359); minor: Changing only `on.push.branches` leaves the trigger comment above it wrong. (Step 11; .github/workflows/ci.yml:40-45); minor: A job that resumes with checks recorded earlier from CI gives the verifier no reuse statement. (Decision 5 / step 8; run/mod.rs:1233-1237 (resumed checks path)); nit: Make sure the fake runs reply exercises the aggregate-job verdict, not only the run's conclusion.
